external_label_and_field_mappings.reason: Preference probing matches the intent; topic IDs and multi-intent arbitration remain unresolved.
A stated need can motivate an argument, but does not identify a valid G1 argumentId.
Reasons about another person may support an argument; neither factual truth nor argument binding follows from the label.
A preference statement is not necessarily an argument or clarification; turn context matters.
Empathy does not necessarily acknowledge a specific established fact.
Cooperation can be proposed without concrete terms or a referenced previous offer.
Undermining a need does not uniquely determine an action or tone.
A fairness claim may endorse or challenge a proposal; context is required.
Rapport and greetings do not imply acknowledgement of a G1 fact.
Absence of a listed strategy is not absence of a canonical action; offers and acceptance can occur here.
Structured event, not a language example; does not distinguish initial from counter-offer or supply internal IDs.
Explicit acceptance event only. Binding to the relevant offer and to any natural utterance is future work.
Explicit exit event only; it is not a gold label for the preceding utterance.
G1 has no standalone objection/reject action. Rejection does not imply walk_away.
Emotion, outcome satisfaction and personality are different from G1 tone; do not infer tone from them.

Null supplies neither an explicit rejection nor an exit intent.

Heuristic question patterns can also occur in proposals; labels are absent from raw data.
Broad agreement/thanks patterns do not resolve factual acknowledgement versus binding acceptance.
Broad numeric/pattern extraction does not establish a valid complete offer.
Reply information is broader than either G1 action; no factual or argument binding follows.
Broad negative patterns and rejection are not a supported standalone G1 action.
Greetings, unknown markers and sequence-control tags do not map to canonical actions.

g1_contract_review.required_bindings: Question topic IDs; acknowledgement fact ID; argument ID; offer terms/conditions; counter-offer target ID; acceptance offer ID; bounded evidence references. These are not supplied by external labels.

mapping_state_definitions.DIRECT_MAPPING: Same intent at the stated annotation/event level. This does not imply a complete G1 action payload or a safe label for adjacent dialogue text.
mapping_state_definitions.NO_SAFE_MAPPING: No reliable label transfer, orthogonal metadata, or no corresponding action in the frozen G1 contract.
mapping_state_definitions.PARTIAL_MAPPING: Overlapping, broader, contextual or multi-intent evidence; no automatic relabeling is justified.

assessment.privacy_limit: Field-level review and Unicode/schema checks are complete. No exhaustive free-text PII screening or redaction was performed; future use of dialogue/reason text requires that review.

quality_findings.detail: Dialogues 35, 428 and 596 each have one unannotated natural-language turn. All 4615 annotation texts exist exactly in their own dialogue, without ambiguous duplicate text, but positional zip alignment would misassign 26 overlapping rows. No repair performed.
Dialogue 19, annotation index 11 has small-talk,self-need,,vouch-fair. One empty comma-delimited token; 10 recognized nonempty labels and 5858 valid label assignments. Raw bytes retained.
Only 396 dialogues have strategy annotations. Strategy labels are multi-label and are not a complete canonical-action inventory. Control markers are not natural utterances.

3935 raw sessions = 2500 completed + 139 terminated + 1296 aborted. Excluding aborted sessions gives the paper count of 2639; the official helper applies task-dependent filters. No filter or split was applied here.
The raw schema has no per-utterance dialogue-act annotations. Paper vocabulary comes from heuristic extraction, not supplied gold labels; act frequencies are unavailable. No extractor was run.
312 sessions have zero comments and 709 have fewer than three. These remain in the immutable raw corpus and raw-session count.

Four bid records in three sessions: Salary 35.5 appears twice in session index 569; Weekly holiday 4.8 appears once in index 1205; one bid omits Salary in index 1777. The fractional values are within numeric bounds but violate the declared INTEGER type.

accepted is true for 2488 bids and null for 4888; no explicit false values. Forty-eight completed sessions have no accepted bid, 26 aborted sessions have accepted bids, and 10 sessions have two accepted bids. Do not derive utterance labels from status or null acceptance.

Raw utility limits are Salary 20..50 and Weekly holiday 2..6. The paper lists weekly days off 2..5; helper constructor limits use 20..51 and 2..7 and get_all_bids uses exclusive range stops. Use the observed raw definitions for this audit; do not silently normalize these differences.

Exact utterance repetition is a statistic, not automatic corruption. CaSiNo has 302 extra repeated language utterances; JI has 9024. JI also has 18 duplicate nonempty role/text dialogue-sequence groups (84 extra sequences). Any later split must prevent group leakage; none created here.

Both sources are English and use different issue vocabularies from Negotiation Arena. Neither is a ready Russian canonical-action corpus. No translation, synthetic generation or target-label conversion was performed.

No G1 tone gold labels exist. CaSiNo emoticons and personal disclosures do not justify tone/personality inference. Demographics, personality, linkable IDs and absolute timestamps are excluded by default as specified in the field review.
